# W2 live Package evidence

PR A: https://github.com/lab255/appliance.sh/pull/174 (merged). PR B: https://github.com/lab255/appliance.sh/pull/177.

**this is now live packaging, not playback**. Both files below were generated by trusted native keyboard activations of the production Workbench Package button, through the Tauri bridge and bundled CLI. Each was separately selected through the shipped `/apps` native Install from file picker, accepted through Unknown Publisher, and installed after the egress-grant prompt. No app was opened or deployed.

Build: W1 main `912c2ae` plus W2 integration; macOS 27.0.1 arm64, Tauri 2.11.2 debug, WebKit, 1280×768 CSS viewport, native reduced motion off. The temporary measurement observer wrapped real calls; it did not substitute results or invoke Package itself. It is recorded as `native-measurement-probe.ts.txt` and removed from shipped code. Screenshots capture only the app window.

## Hand-off integrity

second target = distinct local target namespace on the same host; no second-machine or cloud claim is made. The author workspace records `microvm`; recipient install calls explicitly target `local`. The shipped installer stores immutable bytes locally and target-keyed registry records. A true second-machine demonstration would additionally require a second host with Appliance Runtime, file transfer, its own recipient prompts/registry, and a fresh consumed-byte digest on that host.

The UI digest is the canonical bundle-content digest. ZIP SHA-256 additionally proves exact container bytes. Both columns are recorded values, independently recomputed by the evidence verifier.

## Both user-visible surfaces

| Branch   | Developer Package result                     | Recipient prompt                                                                                                                                                                                                       |

| Unsigned | **“Unsigned — publisher prompts will warn”** | **“Unknown Publisher”**; **“Publisher identity and code origin could not be verified. This does not mean the app is malicious.”**; “Publisher (unverified)”; “Workbench local developer”; **“Signature” / “Unsigned”** |

Captures: [signed Package](native-signed-package.png), [signed publisher](native-signed-publisher.png), [signed grants](native-signed-grants.png), [unsigned Package](native-unsigned-package.png), [unsigned publisher](native-unsigned-publisher.png), [unsigned grants](native-unsigned-grants.png). Verbatim dialog text and full digest attributes are in [native-call-trace.json](native-call-trace.json).

**P2 finding:** signing buys independently verifiable integrity, not recipient trust. Without catalogue binding/resolvable publisher-key evidence, the signed file correctly follows Unknown Publisher. The row shows the **publisher name as declared in the bundle manifest, unverified** (`appliance-runtime-install.ts` assigns `verified.manifest.publisher.name`); no key-derived identity is displayed there. Adjacent title, description and signature text all retain the lack of verification. The two-line row addition was explicitly authorized by the manager; trust/grant decision code and acceptance flags are byte-for-byte unchanged.

## Timing and continuity

Acknowledgment means native trusted Space activation to second animation frame with busy DOM visible: a paint opportunity, not compositor-pixel timing. Backend duration is separately measured from actual host invocation to CLI result. Every sample has `busyBeforeBridge: true`; raw pairs are in [native-timing.json](native-timing.json).

| Configuration                            |   n | Median acknowledgment |                    Paired median backend duration |
| ---------------------------------------- | --: | --------------------: | ------------------------------------------------: |
| Native signed                            |  10 |               74.0 ms |                          391.0 ms, real packaging |
| Native unsigned                          |  10 |               66.5 ms |                          371.0 ms, real packaging |
| Browser fixture Package, no-preference   |  10 |              31.50 ms |      700 ms simulated host delay; no real backend |
| Browser fixture readiness, no-preference |  10 |              30.35 ms | **ZERO backend calls**, pure shell responsiveness |
| Browser fixture Package, reduce          |  10 |              31.65 ms |      700 ms simulated host delay; no real backend |
| Browser fixture readiness, reduce        |  10 |              26.55 ms | **ZERO backend calls**, pure shell responsiveness |

The earlier 28.0/30.2 ms readiness figures also had **ZERO backend calls** and measured only shell responsiveness; the committed final fixture rerun above supersedes them. They must not be compared as equivalent to wave-1 measurements that included real backend work. Browser fixture timing is supplemental, never the live packaging claim.

WebKit reports `layoutShiftSupported: false`; no native CLS number is invented. Chromium fixture results reserve readiness, operation and File rows:

- no-preference: maximum raw layout shift 0.001955; standard CLS 0.001723; footer displacement 0 px; focus remains Package. Readiness arrival CLS 0 and calls 0.
- reduce: maximum raw layout shift 0.001979; standard CLS 0.001746; footer displacement 0 px; focus remains Package. Readiness arrival CLS 0 and calls 0.

The [65-second simulated operation](browser-fixture-slow.json) and 0s/11s/61s captures check reserved space, stage/log/elapsed display and keep-page language; they do not represent a slow real CLI build. Narrow and 200% zoom screenshots are labelled browser fixtures.

## Six properties — S5 Package

| Property    | Evidence / outcome                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ----------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Immediacy   | Pass: synchronous busy-before-await; ten native observations per signing branch, medians under 100 ms, paired backend durations above.                                                             |
| Continuity  | Pass in measured fixture: reserved rows, CLS below 0.01, zero footer movement, focus retained. Native CLS unavailable in WebKit; explicitly limited.                                               |
| Restraint   | Pass: ordinary primary button; no glow/pulse, success motion, auto-next action, or motion-token/spring changes. Reduced-motion fixture retains the same layout.                                    |
| Precision   | Pass: exact unsigned label, source folder/current-snapshot limit, File digest/path, Catalogue coming later, Deploy separate; actual CLI v1 rejection before hand-off.                              |
| Legibility  | Pass in desktop captures plus narrow/200% fixture: long path/digest wrap; reserved File area scrolls; real log disclosure works; signing does not imply trust.                                     |
| Forgiveness | Pass: duplicate click guard; failure clears result, retains real error/log, offers explicit retry; no automatic install/publish/deploy. Keep-page warning and artifact persistence are documented. |

## Boundary call trace and errors

Production chain: human Package handler → `paintPending` busy/paint → `workbenchPackage.package` → Tauri `workbench_package` → bundled `appliance builder package --json` → existing `packageRunnableAppliance` → stages/result. Every measured click produces one Package call. Package result handlers only update UI; installation begins later from explicit `/apps` picker actions. The trace contains no deploy/upload/run calls. Recipient install calls show separate `acceptUnknownPublisher: false`, then `true`, then explicit `grantIds`.

Readiness/registry/result updates have no invocation path into Package. Tests cover zero readiness calls, duplicate suppression, no install/publish/deploy follow-on, error/no File, and explicit retry. MCP registrations remain exactly `overview`, `deploy`, `deployment_status`, `health`, `logs`, `destroy`, `doctor`, `vm` (8). No Package registration or agent-callable method is added. This is a UI/workflow boundary, not containment against arbitrary shell-capable agents (F03).

Native v1 rejection: [trace](native-v1-rejection.json), [capture](native-v1-rejection.png). Engine error: “This is a manifest v1 source project. `appliance package` only emits runnable manifest v2 bundles; use `appliance build` to create the existing source bundle.” No success result followed. CLI tests also exercise a malformed configured signing key: fail, never downgrade.

## Reproduction and limits

Use the committed desktop lock, build/stage the existing CLI, and launch ordinary Tauri dev. Native launch evidence: `Finished dev profile …; Running target/debug/appliance-desktop`. Debug rebuilds can trigger the known Keychain ACL trap; see [recovery instructions](../../workbench-package.md#reproducing-native-development-measurements). Verify recoverable source and `syncedKeyId`, quit, delete only affected recoverable desktop items, clear the corresponding field, and let the app recreate its own keys. Never recreate with `security add-generic-password`.

F01: provisioning UI and publisher trust distribution deferred; detect-and-use only. F03: no new MCP authority filter or shell containment. F05: local immutable storage plus target-keyed record, no remote/cloud ingestion claim. F08: catalogue publication, buildSet fan-out and package/compound promotion deferred. Readiness proposals are not synthesized from session completion; production manual Package works without one.

The separate CI `--locked` guard was delivered as worker commit `1d0ba55`, manager republished `d0a63f1` on `bb/w2-desktop-lock-guard`; publication is owner-blocked by GitHub PAT workflow scope. It does not block the Package implementation.

## Integrated validation

```text
pnpm verify
==> verify: GREEN
App: 27 test files, 140 tests passed
Desktop: 6 test files, 50 tests passed
VM suite: 330 passed, 0 failed
cargo test --locked --manifest-path packages/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml --lib workbench_package
1 passed; 0 failed; 60 filtered out
```

The first sandboxed verify attempt could not write existing VM fixtures under
`~/.appliance`; the complete rerun with fixture access passed. No implementation
change or lockfile refresh was used to make it pass. Registry springs,
`ff-manifest`, motion tokens and MCP registration source are untouched.

## Final W3 integration

Rebased onto merged W3 main `882c995`. Four conflicts were reported before
resolution: adjacent imports/exports in app index, app host and desktop host, plus
the detail-shell inspector/action seam. The final diff preserves W3’s live
`WorkspaceInspector`, `ConsoleHost extends InspectionHost`, native inspection
commands and async workspace commands. Package replaces only the action placeholder
below the inspector. All 24 other W3 files are byte-for-byte unchanged from main,
including its mount guard implementation and Cargo dependency changes.

The native measurements/captures above remain explicitly attributed to W1 plus W2
before this rebase. The Package engine, bridge, component and recipient dialog code
did not change; the surrounding inspector composition did. They are not relabelled
as fresh measurements of the W3 inspector.

Final combined-state validation: `pnpm verify` GREEN after rebuilding stale app
declarations; `cargo test --locked --manifest-path
packages/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml --lib`: **72 passed, 0 failed**.

Prior-head GitHub CI used Rust 1.100 and rejected the existing VM doctor's
`if predicate { return true; } false` with `clippy::needless_bool`. A separate main-based CI compatibility PR replaces that with the identical
predicate expression; it is excluded from this Package branch. No redaction
decision changes. The prior CI logs identify `src/doctor.rs:623` in
both Rust verification and Windows desktop jobs.
